quizzes.title: Capital Cities
quizzes.description: Match the country to its capital in this friendly world tour.

questions.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.note: Kyoto was the imperial capital for more than a thousand years before Tokyo.

questions.q: Sydney is the capital of Australia.
questions.note: The capital is Canberra, purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.note: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.

questions.q: What is the capital of Italy?
questions.note: Vatican City, the world's smallest country, sits inside Rome.

questions.q: What is the capital of Egypt?
questions.note: The Pyramids of Giza stand on the edge of greater Cairo.

questions.q: What is the capital of Germany?
questions.note: Bonn was the capital of West Germany before reunification.

questions.q: Madrid is the capital of Spain.
questions.note: Madrid sits almost exactly in the centre of Spain.

questions.q: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.note: Brasília was purpose-built and replaced Rio as capital in 1960.

questions.q: What is the capital of Russia?
questions.note: The Kremlin, Russia's seat of government, is in the heart of Moscow.

questions.q: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.note: Kampala is Uganda's capital and Addis Ababa is Ethiopia's.

quizzes.title: Peaks & Rivers
quizzes.description: From the Alps to the Amazon, test your knowledge of great rivers and mountains.

questions.q: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.note: The Tigris and Euphrates together defined ancient Mesopotamia.

questions.q: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?
questions.note: It is Africa's highest mountain.

questions.q: The Amazon River flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.note: It carries more water than any other river on Earth.

questions.q: Which Russian mountain range is traditionally seen as the boundary between Europe and Asia?
questions.note: Accept Ural Mountains.

questions.q: Which river flows through Paris?
questions.note: The banks of the Seine in Paris are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: The Matterhorn sits on the border between Switzerland and which country?
questions.note: In Italy the mountain is known as Monte Cervino.

questions.q: The River Rhine flows into the Mediterranean Sea.
questions.note: The Rhine empties into the North Sea through the Netherlands.

questions.q: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and which country?
questions.note: The northern side of Everest is in Tibet, an autonomous region of China.

questions.q: What is the longest river in Europe?
questions.note: The Volga flows entirely through Russia into the Caspian Sea.

questions.q: Which of these capital cities lies on the River Danube?
questions.note: Vienna, Bratislava and Belgrade also stand on the Danube.

quizzes.title: Seas & Isles
quizzes.description: Dive into the world's oceans, seas, straits and island nations.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.note: The Pacific covers more area than all of Earth's land put together.

questions.q: Not counting continental Australia, what is the world's largest island?
questions.note: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

questions.q: Madagascar lies off the east coast of Africa.
questions.note: Most of its wildlife, including lemurs, is found nowhere else on Earth.

questions.q: What is the smallest of the world's five oceans?
questions.note: Accept Arctic Ocean; much of it is covered by sea ice.

questions.q: The Galápagos Islands belong to which country?
questions.note: Their wildlife helped inspire Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.

questions.q: Which body of water is so salty that people float in it with ease?
questions.note: Its shore is the lowest point on dry land on Earth.

questions.q: Tasmania is an island state of New Zealand.
questions.note: Tasmania is a state of Australia.

questions.q: Which US state is made up entirely of islands in the Pacific Ocean?
questions.note: It became the 50th US state in 1959.

questions.q: The Strait of Gibraltar links the Atlantic Ocean with which sea?
questions.note: At its narrowest it is only about 14 km wide.

questions.q: Which ocean lies between the east coast of Africa and the west coast of Australia?
questions.note: It is the only ocean named after a country.

quizzes.title: Borders & Neighbours
quizzes.description: Enclaves, landlocked nations and shared frontiers for true map lovers.

questions.q: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.note: Lesotho is the only country whose entire territory lies above 1,000 metres.

questions.q: Which two countries share the world's longest international border?
questions.note: It runs for nearly 9,000 km, including the Alaska section.

questions.q: Paraguay has a coastline on the Pacific Ocean.
questions.note: Paraguay is landlocked, as is its neighbour Bolivia.

questions.q: Which small country lies between Spain and France in the Pyrenees?
questions.note: Andorra's capital, Andorra la Vella, is the highest capital city in Europe.

questions.q: Apart from Vatican City, which country is entirely surrounded by Italy?
questions.note: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic.

questions.q: Which of these countries does not share a border with Brazil?
questions.note: Chile and Ecuador are the only South American countries not bordering Brazil.

questions.q: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
questions.note: It is also the ninth-largest country overall.

questions.q: The Khyber Pass links Pakistan with which country?
questions.note: For centuries it was a key route for traders and invading armies.

questions.q: Which country lies on both sides of the Bosporus strait?
questions.note: Accept Türkiye; the Bosporus splits Istanbul between Europe and Asia.

questions.q: Which country borders both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.note: Iran is the only country with coastlines on both.
